A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NegationCLIP study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Existing supplementary material can be matched across reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original corpus analyses, CLIP benchmark results, ablations, text-to-image generation and segmentation experiments, including supplementary CelebA and LMD results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds SigLIP experiments in Appendix E, Table 10.

M1.justification: The two caption-generation pipelines, CLIP text-encoder fine-tuning procedure, and downstream encoder substitution are unchanged. The SigLIP experiment reports application of the existing approach without specifying an algorithmic adaptation.

E1.justification: Training, evaluation, and corpus-analysis coverage is retained. The added SigLIP experiment uses the existing VALSE, NegRefCOCOg, ImageNet, and COCO benchmarks without introducing another dataset, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: v3 Table 10 adds SigLIP as the comparator for Neg.SigLIP at base, large, and so400m scales. Existing comparison sets are unchanged, including the LMD comparison already present in v2 Table 12.

E3.justification: The added experiment evaluates SigLIP base, large, and so400m configurations. Existing CLIP settings, data splits, metrics, and downstream testing procedures are retained; no revisions to those experiments' protocols are reported.

E4.justification: New Appendix E tests whether the approach's benefits extend beyond CLIP by comparing SigLIP and Neg.SigLIP at three scales. This adds a limited check of generality across model families; existing caption ablations, case studies, and qualitative failure examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging text-to-image results over five random seeds. The SigLIP table adds point estimates without introducing run-count information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds SigLIP/Neg.SigLIP results at three scales. For example, Table 10 reports base-model VALSE scores of 67.98/77.15 and NegRefCOCOg scores of 61.59/68.18. Existing results remain unchanged, including the relocated LMD scores of 20%, 94%, and 100%.

T1.justification: NegRefCOCOg's patch definitions, non-overlap equations, and expansion constraints are unchanged. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs accompany the SigLIP results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about negation-inclusive data generation, NegRefCOCOg, improved negation comprehension, and downstream applicability.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly interprets the SigLIP results as evidence that the approach is model-agnostic and preserves general performance. Existing explanations and limitations, including dual-encoder alignment concerns and failures on strongly associated concepts, are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project repository link on the title page. Existing prompts, hyperparameters, hardware information, and segmentation thresholds are retained when Experiment Details moves from Appendix E to G. SigLIP-specific fine-tuning details are not supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to SigLIP, FLUX, diffusion training, and two segmentation/regional-understanding works, while removing the original VQA and ImageNet challenge references. These mainly revise introductory citations; Section 6's substantive positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds a brief additional-models appendix and acknowledgements, updates affiliation information, and reorders supplementary sections. Experiment Details moves from E to G and Additional Qualitative Results from G to H. Most prose and the main narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds SigLIP Table 10 and moves the existing LMD table from a standalone final page to its discussion in Appendix F, renumbering it Table 11. Prompt tables are renumbered and appendix layout reflows; Figures 1–9 retain their content.

improvement.justification: Appendix E provides useful additional evidence that the approach works with SigLIP, extending v2's CLIP-focused validation. The repository link and placement of the LMD table beside its discussion improve usability. These are limited gains: the core study is unchanged, and the added experiment lacks SigLIP-specific training details and uncertainty estimates.
